title: Myself, yourself: reflexive verbs
title_target: Sara ska gifta sig i augusti!
goal: Use the everyday verbs that need *mig, dig, sig, oss, er* in Swedish even when English needs no "myself" at all.
bekal: you can choose the right reflexive pronoun for every person: *mig, dig, sig, oss, er, sig*
you can tell action from position: *sätta sig* / *sitta*, *lägga sig* / *ligga*
you can talk about getting ready, feeling and getting married: *klä på sig*, *känna sig*, *gifta sig*
wave: Go back to Unit 5: read the s-passive sentences aloud (*Kaffet serveras klockan åtta*, *Huset byggdes 1890* …) and turn each one into an active sentence with *man*: *Man serverar kaffet klockan åtta*.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Brunch hos Anna och Lars
dialogs.intro: Saturday brunch at Elin and Jonas's parents, Anna and Lars. The three flatmates from Södermalm arrive twenty minutes late, and Anna has news about Sara, Elin and Jonas's cousin.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Kom in, kom in! Sätt er, maten är klar.
lines.id: Come in, come in! Sit down, the food's ready.
lines.literal: come in, come in! set yourselves, food-the is ready.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Förlåt att vi är sena. Jag försov mig.
lines.literal: sorry that we are late. I over-slept myself.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Igen? När lade du dig egentligen?
lines.id: Again? What time did you actually go to bed?
lines.literal: again? when laid you yourself actually?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Klockan tre. Bandet övade till två, och sedan cyklade jag hem.
lines.id: At three. The band practiced until two, and then I biked home.
lines.literal: clock-the three. band-the practiced till two, and then biked I home.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Och du, Dian? Hur känner du dig i den nya lägenheten?
lines.id: And you, Dian? How do you feel in the new flat?
lines.literal: and you, Dian? how feel you yourself in the new flat-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jättebra. Jag har vant mig vid allt, till och med Jonas gitarr.
lines.id: Great. I've gotten used to everything, even Jonas's guitar.
lines.literal: giant-good. I have accustomed myself to everything, even Jonas guitar.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Bra. Vi har förresten nyheter. Berätta du, Anna.
lines.id: Good. We have some news, by the way. You tell them, Anna.
lines.literal: good. we have by-the-way news. tell you, Anna.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Sara ska gifta sig i augusti!
lines.literal: Sara shall marry herself in August!

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Med Ali, killen från Lund. De förlovade sig i julas.
lines.id: To Ali, the guy from Lund. They got engaged last Christmas.
lines.literal: with Ali, guy-the from Lund. they engaged themselves in Christmas.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Och ni är bjudna allihop, Dian också.
lines.id: And you're all invited, Dian too.
lines.literal: and you are invited all-up, Dian also.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Vad roligt! Men jag har aldrig varit på ett svenskt bröllop. Vad har man på sig?
lines.id: How lovely! But I've never been to a Swedish wedding. What do people wear?
lines.literal: what fun! but I have never been at a Swedish wedding. what has one on oneself?

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Klä upp dig lite, men inte för mycket. Och förbered dig på många tal.
lines.id: Dress up a little, but not too much. And be ready for lots of speeches.
lines.literal: dress up yourself a-little, but not too much. and prepare yourself on many speeches.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Och lär dig en snapsvisa. Alla sjunger på svenska bröllop.
lines.id: And learn a drinking song. Everybody sings at Swedish weddings.
lines.literal: and teach yourself a schnapps-song. all sing at Swedish weddings.

lines.speaker: Lars:
lines.text: Nu sätter vi oss och äter, innan maten blir kall.
lines.id: Now let's sit down and eat, before the food gets cold.
lines.literal: now set we ourselves and eat, before food-the becomes cold.

notes: **Sätt er** — Anna is talking to three people, so the reflexive pronoun is *er* ("yourselves"). To one person she would say *Sätt dig*. The reflexive pronoun always matches the subject, and Swedish has six of them: *mig, dig, sig, oss, er, sig*, pronounced **may, day, say, os, ehr, say**.

**Jag försov mig** — "I overslept". English needs no "myself" here, but Swedish insists on it. Many everyday Swedish verbs work like this: *försova sig* (oversleep), *skynda sig* (hurry), *känna sig* (feel), *gifta sig* (get married), *vänja sig* (get used to). Learn them **with** *sig*, the way you learn nouns with *en* or *ett*. *Försova* is strong, like *sova*: *försov*, *har försovit*.

**När lade du dig?** — *lägga sig* means "to lie down, to go to bed" (an action), while *ligga* means "to be lying" (a position). In speech, the past *lade* is almost always shortened to **la** (**lah**): *jag la mig klockan tre*. Both spellings are correct; *lade* is the more formal one.

**Jag har vant mig vid** — *vänja sig vid* is "to get used to": *vande*, *har vant*. And *Jonas gitarr* is "Jonas's guitar": a name that already ends in *-s* takes no extra *s* and, in standard Swedish, no apostrophe either — *Jonas gitarr*, *Lars bil*.

**Gifta sig med** — you don't "marry somebody" in Swedish, you "marry yourself with" them: *Sara ska gifta sig **med** Ali*. The state is the participle from Unit 6: *hon är **gift*** (married), *de är **förlovade*** (engaged). **I julas** ("last Christmas") belongs to the *i fredags*, *i somras* family: always past.

**Tal** and **snapsvisor** — a Swedish wedding dinner is led by a *toastmaster* (or *toastmadame*), and the speeches can go on for hours: parents, siblings, best friends, colleagues. Between them, guests sing *snapsvisor*, short drinking songs printed in the program. **Lär dig** here means "learn": *lära sig* = to learn, but *lära* alone = to teach — *Lena lär oss svenska* (Lena teaches us Swedish), *vi lär oss svenska* (we learn Swedish).

grammars.title: The reflexive pronouns
body: Here is one verb, *sätta sig* (to sit down), with every person. Only the first and the last column change together.
after: For *jag, du, vi, ni* the reflexive pronoun is just the ordinary object pronoun you already know. Only the third person has a special word, **sig** — and it matters: *Han tvättar **sig*** (he washes himself) but *Han tvättar **honom*** (he washes someone else, another man). It is the same logic as *sin* vs *hans* from Unit 10 of Svenska 101.

Word order: the reflexive pronoun follows the verb, and after inversion it follows the subject: *Nu sätter **vi oss***. *Igår la **jag mig** sent*. In the perfect tense it follows the supine: *Jag har **försovit mig***.
In a subordinate clause BIFF still applies, and *inte* goes before the verb: *…eftersom jag **inte känner mig** frisk*.

grammars.title: Swedish says sig, English doesn't
body: The verbs below are reflexive in Swedish but not in English. Learn the left column as a unit, *sig* included.
after: The first three come in pairs with the position verbs you know: **sitta – sätta sig**, **ligga – lägga sig**, **stå – ställa sig**. The reflexive one is the movement, the plain one is the position: *Jag **sätter mig** i soffan* (I sit down) → *nu **sitter** jag i soffan* (now I'm sitting). Never say *jag sitter mig*.

blocks.text: Some morning-routine verbs are reflexive in Swedish, some are not — and it is not always the ones you would guess. Read the table aloud as a little story: first you wake up, last you rush out the door.

blocks.title: Three ways to talk about clothes
items: **ta på sig** = put on (an action, Unit 3): *Ta på dig jackan, det är kallt.*
**ha på sig** = wear, have on (a state): *Vad har man på sig på ett bröllop?*
**klä upp sig** = dress up: *Klä upp dig lite!* And **klä om sig** = change clothes: *Jag måste klä om mig efter jobbet.*

blocks.text: Swedish weddings are usually in summer, often in a small country church followed by a long dinner. Guests are expected to stay until late, and one tradition surprises many visitors: when the groom leaves the room, the male guests may line up to kiss the bride on the cheek — and the same goes the other way round. When someone taps a glass with a knife, it is not always a toast: it may be a request for silence before the next *tal*.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 6
items: Say what happened, then the state: *De gifte sig* → *De är gifta*. *De förlovade sig* → *De är förlovade*. *Vi blev bjudna* → *Vi är bjudna*.
Make the participles agree: *en gift man*, *ett gift par*, *två gifta par*.

vocab.en: to lie down, to go to bed
to stand (somewhere), to get in line
